title: India and Spain to Fast-Track UPI-Bizum Interoperability Talks
excerpt: As RBI expands UPI's global footprint and Europe's Bizum network consolidates, India and Spain are accelerating discussions to link their real-time payment systems for cross-border transactions.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • India and Spain are fast-tracking talks to link UPI with Bizum for cross-border payments.
  • UPI processes over 20 billion transactions monthly and is live in over eight countries.
  • Bizum is expanding into a pan-European network covering 13 countries and 130 million users.
  • The UPI-Bizum link could significantly reduce transfer costs for users in both countries.
  • India has signed agreements with 23 countries to enhance its digital payment infrastructure.
  • India and Spain are accelerating discussions to link UPI with Spain's Bizum mobile payment system, building on growing bilateral digital cooperation.
  • The RBI has entered the implementation phase of linking UPI with Europe's TIPS instant payment system alongside NPCI International Payments Ltd.
  • Bizum is consolidating into a pan-European payment network covering 13 countries and up to 130 million users, making it a natural gateway for UPI into the eurozone.
  • UPI is now live in over eight countries including France, Singapore, and the UAE, and processes more than 20 billion transactions monthly.

India and Spain are moving to fast-track talks on linking their flagship digital payment platforms — UPI and Bizum — as both countries deepen their technological partnership and seek to reduce cross-border payment friction for millions of users.

The push comes at a moment when India's Unified Payments Interface is rapidly expanding its global footprint and Spain's Bizum is consolidating its position as the backbone of a pan-European mobile payment network. During Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez's visit to India, he used UPI to make a payment in Mumbai — a gesture that the Ministry of External Affairs described as "experiencing India's digital revolution first hand" and a sign that "digital pathways are fast connecting India-Spain technological partnership."

RBI Pushes UPI Into Europe

The Reserve Bank of India has already entered the implementation phase of linking UPI with Europe's TARGET Instant Payment Settlement (TIPS) system, operated by the European Central Bank. NPCI International Payments Ltd (NIPL), the overseas arm of India's National Payments Corporation, is leading the technical integration alongside the ECB.

"But with both platforms scaling aggressively — UPI processes over 20 billion transactions monthly, while Bizum is expanding across the EU — the commercial logic is hard to ignore."

"Reserve Bank of India and NIPL will continue to collaborate closely with European Central Bank to operationalize the UPI–TIPS link, including technical integration, risk management and settlement arrangements," the RBI said in a recent statement.

The UPI-TIPS interlinkage is expected to sharply reduce transfer costs and settlement friction for the millions of Indians who send or receive money across the eurozone. It would also boost merchant acceptance for Indian travellers in Europe, similar to the QR-based rollouts already operational in Singapore and the UAE.

Bizum's Pan-European Ambitions

On the Spanish side, Bizum is no longer just a domestic success story. The mobile payment platform — used by the vast majority of Spanish smartphone owners — has signed interoperability agreements with Italy's Bancomat Pay and Portugal's SIBS-MBWay. Together with France's EPI and Scandinavia's VIPPS MobilePay, these systems are building a continent-wide payment network covering 13 countries and potentially 130 million users, with cross-border personal transfers launching in 2026 and in-store payments planned for 2027.

A report by Spain's Nuek, part of the Indra Group, found that Spain has consolidated its position as "a European benchmark for the adoption of instant peer-to-peer payments and the digitalization of international remittances." Spain is considered a strong candidate to host the central headquarters of the pan-European Bizum network.

What Interoperability Would Mean

Linking UPI with Bizum — either directly or through the broader UPI-TIPS corridor — would create a seamless payment bridge between India's 504-million-strong user base and Spain's digitally mature consumer market. For Indian travellers, it would mean paying at Spanish restaurants, shops, and transit systems using familiar UPI apps like Google Pay, PhonePe, or BHIM. For businesses, it would open a low-cost channel for trade settlements and invoice payments.

"The proposed UPI–TIPS initiative is more than a payments link; it is a signal of India's emergence as a global benchmark for real-time payments," said Akash Sinha, CEO of Cashfree Payments. "For fintechs, this marks the beginning of a new era where Indian payment infrastructure is not just world-class, but globally interconnected."

The Diaspora Dividend

For the estimated 50,000-strong Indian community in Spain — and the growing number of Indian students choosing Spanish universities — UPI-Bizum interoperability would be transformative. Currently, sending money between India and Spain involves wire transfers or services like Wise and Western Union, with fees that can run between 2 and 5 per cent per transaction. A linked system could bring those costs down to a fraction, as has already happened in UPI's corridors with Singapore and the UAE.

India has signed memorandums of understanding with 23 countries for sharing or cooperation on the India Stack, its suite of digital public infrastructure. UPI is now live in over eight countries, including the UAE, Singapore, Bhutan, Nepal, Sri Lanka, France, Mauritius, and Qatar. Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal recently witnessed the launch of UPI services in Greece through a partnership between Eurobank and NIPL.

What's Next

The timeline for a formal UPI-Bizum link remains fluid. Technical integration, regulatory harmonisation across Indian and European frameworks, and settlement currency arrangements all need to be resolved. But with both platforms scaling aggressively — UPI processes over 20 billion transactions monthly, while Bizum is expanding across the EU — the commercial logic is hard to ignore. The next concrete milestone will likely come when NIPL and the Spanish banking consortium behind Bizum formalise a technical roadmap, expected to take shape in the coming months.
